title: MEPS 2024 financial room and medical debt align with cost-related care delay measures
source_unit: MEPS 2024 person-level financial-room, medical-debt, and cost-related care-access fields

observations.period: 2024; round 4/2 financial room, medical debt, and cost-related care access

denominator.unit: HC-256 person records before field-specific valid denominators; weighted estimates use positive PERWT24F

confidence_categories.value: not at all, not too, somewhat, and very confident paying an unexpected expense

care_delay_and_affordability.value: medical-care and prescription delay/inability-to-afford shares by confidence and medical-debt group

medical_care_delay_not_confident.unit: percent among respondents not confident paying an unexpected expense

medical_care_delay_confident.unit: percent among respondents confident paying an unexpected expense

medical_care_delay_any_medical_debt.unit: percent among respondents with any medical debt

medical_care_delay_no_medical_debt.unit: percent among respondents with no medical debt

medical_care_delay_10001_to_20000_debt.unit: percent among respondents reporting $10,001-$20,000 medical debt

medical_care_delay_5001_to_10000_debt.unit: percent among respondents reporting $5,001-$10,000 medical debt

observations.method: Cross-tab valid financial-room and medical-debt categories against cost-related medical-care and prescription access fields using positive PERWT24F.
observations.uncertainty: The fields need not refer to the same bill or need and do not establish timing, causation, alternatives, completion, remedy, trust, or action; amount-band cells vary in size and are not event-specific.
observations.subgroup: MEPS 2024 respondents with valid field-specific values; confidence and debt groups retained separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: Common illness, age, coverage, access, prior debt, and reporting differences can generate the observed association.

boundary: This is a same-respondent cross-sectional association between financial room/medical debt and cost-related care access. It does not identify a dated episode, causal effect, household adaptation, remedy, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
